title: Unique identifier linking in user data store
description: The MongoDB users collection stores parent account data containing unique identifiers (user IDs, account IDs) that can link data to specific individuals across the system.

title: Quasi-identifier combination in user data
description: Parent account data may contain combinations of attributes (email, username, etc.) that can serve as quasi-identifiers, enabling linking of data to individuals through attribute combination.

title: Processing of identified parent account data
description: The system requests and processes identified data (parent account information) which directly identifies data subjects.

title: Unique identifier in user account data
description: The MongoDB users collection contains unique references to the identity of data subjects through user account identifiers.

title: Quasi-identifier in parent account data
description: Parent account data may contain combinations of attributes that are unique to a data subject, enabling identification through quasi-identifiers.

title: Attributable data evidence from stored accounts
description: Stored parent account data can be used to prevent individuals from denying certain claims or actions associated with their account.

title: Potentially sensitive parent account data types
description: Parent account data may be perceived as highly sensitive and should only be collected and processed when strictly required by the authentication service functionality.

title: Data retention beyond functional need
description: Parent account data may be stored in the MongoDB collection longer than functionally needed for the authentication service's operational requirements.

title: Excessive party access to stored account data
description: Parent account data may be made accessible to more parties than functionally necessary, including system administrators, backup services, or other internal services.

title: Unawareness of parent account data storage
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their parent account information is being collected, stored, and processed by the authentication service.

title: Lack of user control over data processing preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their parent account data is processed, stored, or retained.

title: Limited control over data rectification and erasure
description: Data subjects may lack adequate control to rectify incorrect parent account data or remove personal data that is no longer relevant.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data may be processed than is actually needed for the authentication service's functional goals, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.

title: Potential violation of storage limitation principle
description: Parent account data may be stored longer than needed, potentially violating GDPR storage limitation requirements.

title: Insufficient data subject controls for privacy rights
description: Support for different data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure) may be lacking for the stored parent account data.

title: JWT Token Contains Unique Identifier
description: JWT tokens typically contain unique user identifiers that can be used to link data across systems and sessions, potentially enabling tracking of user activities.
assumptions: JWT tokens are transmitted in clear or can be intercepted
uncertainty_note: Assuming JWT contains user identifier claims

title: User Identity Revealed in JWT
description: JWT tokens contain user identity information that can be extracted and used to identify the data subject, potentially exposing personal information to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: JWT contains user identity claims
uncertainty_note: Assuming JWT contains identifiable user information

title: Excessive User Data Disclosure
description: User data transmitted alongside JWT may include more sensitive information than functionally required for the authentication service to parent user interaction.
assumptions: User data contains sensitive personal information
uncertainty_note: Assuming user data includes sensitive fields

title: Linking through parent email identifier
description: Parent email serves as a unique identifier that can link the child's login activity to the parent's identity, potentially exposing the child's usage patterns to the parent or third parties.
assumptions: Email addresses are typically unique identifiers

title: Quasi-identifier combination through email and password
description: The combination of parent email and password can serve as quasi-identifiers that may uniquely identify the child user across systems or contexts.
assumptions: Email+password combination may be unique enough to identify individuals

title: Processing of identified data
description: The authentication service processes identified personal data (parent email and password) to authenticate the child user, which directly identifies the data subject.
assumptions: Email and password are clearly identifiable personal data

title: Identifier processing - parent email
description: Parent email is processed as an identifier that directly references the identity of the parent data subject, even though the child is the user.
assumptions: Email is a standard identifier for individuals

title: Sensitive data type collection - password
description: Password is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly necessary. The flow involves password transmission which carries significant privacy risk.
assumptions: Passwords are among the most sensitive personal data types

title: Unnecessary data treatment - password storage
description: Passwords should not be stored or processed beyond what is needed for authentication. Extended processing or storage of passwords beyond authentication purposes creates privacy risks.
assumptions: Passwords should be hashed and not stored in plaintext

title: Child unawareness of data processing
description: The child user may not be fully aware that their login activity is linked to parent identity through email, or that their authentication data is being processed and stored.
assumptions: Children may not understand privacy implications of data collection

title: Limited control over data processing preferences
description: The child user has limited control over how their authentication data is processed, stored, or shared with the authentication service.
assumptions: Children typically have limited privacy controls

title: Data minimization violation - parent email for child login
description: Collecting parent email for child authentication may violate data minimization principles if the parent email is not strictly necessary for the child's login functionality.
assumptions: Parent email may not be functionally required for child authentication

title: Potential invalid consent for child data processing
description: Children may not provide valid consent for processing their personal data, especially when linked to parent identity through email authentication.
assumptions: Children's consent capacity is legally limited

title: Data exposure to predetermined parties
description: Authentication service may share authentication data with predetermined third parties (e.g., analytics, compliance, or partner services) beyond what is functionally necessary for authentication.
assumptions: Authentication services often have data sharing agreements

title: Lawfulness problems - automated authentication decisions
description: Automated authentication decisions based on child's login may raise lawfulness concerns, especially when linked to parent identity and potentially affecting access to services.
assumptions: Automated decisions may have legal implications

title: Linking through unique user identifiers
description: Child User interactions (video search, request, like, comment) are linked to the user through unique identifiers (user IDs, account IDs) that persist across all interactions in the Video Management Service.
assumptions: The system maintains persistent user accounts with unique identifiers.

title: Profiling individual through video search and interaction patterns
description: Video search queries, likes, and comments can be analyzed to create profiles of individual users, revealing preferences, interests, and potentially sensitive information about the user.
assumptions: The system collects and stores historical interaction data for analysis.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The Video Management Service processes identified data including user identifiers associated with video search, requests, likes, and comments.
assumptions: User accounts and identifiers are required for all interactions.

title: Revealing attributes through video content and interactions
description: Video search queries, comments, and like patterns may reveal personal attributes about the user such as interests, location preferences, or other sensitive information.
assumptions: Video content and user interactions contain or imply personal information.

title: Data type sensitivity - video content collection
description: Video content and associated metadata may be more sensitive than functionally required for basic video search and interaction functionality.
assumptions: Video data collection extends beyond what is strictly necessary for the stated functionality.

title: Unnecessary treatment and analysis of video data
description: Video data may be further treated, analyzed, and enriched (e.g., for recommendations, analytics) beyond what is necessary to achieve the functional goals of video search, request, like, and comment.
assumptions: The system performs additional processing on video data beyond core functionality.

title: Unawareness of data processing by data subject
description: Child Users may not be fully aware of all data collection, processing, and storage activities associated with video search, likes, and comments.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not comprehensively describe all data processing activities.

title: Lack of control over data processing preferences
description: Users may lack adequate control to set preferences or consent regarding how their video search, like, and comment data is processed, stored, and shared.
assumptions: Privacy settings and consent mechanisms may be limited or difficult to use.

title: Lack of control for rectification and erasure
description: Users may not have adequate mechanisms to correct incorrect data or remove personal data that is no longer relevant from video search, like, and comment activities.
assumptions: Data retention and deletion mechanisms may be insufficient.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data may be processed than is actually needed for video search, request, like, and comment functionality, violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: Data collection and processing may exceed functional requirements.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Personal data from video interactions may be stored longer than functionally needed, violating GDPR storage limitation requirements.
assumptions: Data retention policies may not align with functional necessity.

title: Sensitive video data type collected
description: Video data is highly sensitive personal data that may be collected and processed beyond what is functionally required for streaming approved video to a child.

title: Excessive video granularity
description: Video data may be disclosed at a more fine-grained level of granularity than needed for the intended purpose of streaming approved video to a child.

title: Unnecessary video processing
description: Video data may be further treated, analyzed, or enriched in ways not necessary to achieve the functionality of streaming approved video to a child.

title: Data shared with predetermined parties
description: Video data is made accessible to a predetermined set of parties (the child user) which may be more than functionally necessary.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The system requests and processes identified data (video) that can be associated with the child user.

title: Revealing attributes in video
description: Video data may include revealing attributes that support identification of the data subject (child user).

title: Quasi-identifier combining in video
description: Video data may contain combinations of attributes (e.g., location, time, context) that can serve as quasi-identifiers to link data to an individual.

title: Profiling through video analysis
description: Personal data of an individual can be analyzed for patterns to link data to that individual through video content.

title: Unawareness of video processing
description: The child user may not be fully aware about the collection, processing, storage, or disclosure of their personal data in the video stream.

title: Lack of control over video preferences
description: The child user may lack control to set preferences or consent in how personal data is processed (or collected/stored) in the video stream.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (video) is processed than is actually needed for the functional goal of streaming approved video to a child.

title: Invalid consent for video processing
description: Personal data collection and processing may not rely on valid consent from the child user or their guardian.

title: Linking through unique identifiers in child profiles
description: The MongoDB childprofiles collection likely contains unique identifiers (user IDs, account IDs) that can be used to link browsing data to specific children, enabling cross-referencing and tracking across systems.

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Child browsing data typically contains multiple attributes (timestamp, page views, duration, device type) that can be combined to create quasi-identifiers, potentially enabling re-identification of individual children.

title: Profiling an individual through browsing patterns
description: The AI Recommendation Engine will analyze child browsing patterns to create behavioral profiles, which can be used to link data to specific individuals and infer sensitive characteristics.

title: Processing of quasi-identifiable browsing data
description: Child browsing data contains combinations of attributes that are unique to individual data subjects, making the data identifiable even without explicit identifiers.

title: Revealing attributes in browsing data
description: Browsing patterns can reveal sensitive information about children's interests, preferences, and potentially their location or circumstances, supporting identification of the data subject.

title: Sensitive data type collection for children
description: Child browsing data is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required, especially given the special protection status of children's data under privacy regulations.

title: Excessive AI processing and analysis
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may perform analysis, enrichment, and transformation of child browsing data beyond what is functionally necessary for the stated recommendation purpose.

title: Data propagation to AI services
description: Child browsing data is propagated to the AI Recommendation Engine where it may be accessible by or shared with other services where it is not strictly needed.

title: Unawareness of data processing by children/parents
description: Children and their guardians may not be aware that their browsing data is being collected, processed, and sent to an AI engine for analysis and profiling.

title: Lack of control over data processing preferences
description: Children and parents may lack control to set preferences or provide consent regarding how their child's browsing data is processed, stored, and analyzed by the AI engine.

title: Lack of rectification and erasure control
description: Children and parents may lack the ability to rectify incorrect browsing data or request erasure of their child's data once it has been processed by the AI engine.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Child browsing data may be processed in excess of what is actually needed for the functional goal of the AI Recommendation Engine, violating the data minimization principle.

title: Automated decision-making on children's data
description: The AI Recommendation Engine performs automated decision-making based on children's personal data, which may raise lawfulness problems under regulations like GDPR, especially given the special protection for children's data.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Child browsing data may be stored longer than functionally needed, particularly given the sensitive nature of children's data and the requirement for strict storage limitation.
